after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}\,0 & \,1 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}\,0 & \,1 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}\,0 & \,1 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,0 & \,1 \\ \,\,-2 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +9 & =0 \\ (\lambda -9)(\lambda -1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$

content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Square Matrix
content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}0-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )((5-\lambda )(8-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +36) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )[(8-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-4)]+2(-2)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)+(-4)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )[(8-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-4)]+2(-2)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)+(-4)(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}

content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((5-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +9) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(\lambda -1)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$
